note: v1 91.54 (seeds 0/11 91.54/91.54): CALL AND RETURN - first draft of an ELECTRO FUGUE MACHINE. An eight-bar subject over a four-bar loop (i - VI - iv - V), written so it canons against itself four bars later, is taken up in turn by an FM bell (phase modulation 3.5:1), a hard-synced lead, a PWM wavetable pulse and an FM bass over a motorik machine kit; then the machine starts CALLING: a seeded grammar pushes and pops a call stack every four bars, and each level spawns a faster copy of the current bar an octave higher (sixteenths, thirty-seconds, then sixty-fourths blurring into a glass shimmer) - the texture's density and level follow the stack; each calls section RETURNS (the stack empties, the drums pull back to a kick and a rim fill). The canon modulates - D minor, G minor (an electro-break kick, the pulse arpeggiating, the sync lead resting), A minor (half time, the voices crossed) - all tuned in WERCKMEISTER III, a well temperament, so each key has its own colour; then a return (the subject alone, augmented, on the bell), a final call that fills the stack to the top and unwinds, and an outro of bell tolls. 152 bars at 120 bpm, 5:04. Weakest term: rhythm (the quantised machine has no off-grid share; I will humanize it next). Not heard by me.

v2 92.24 (seed 0; v1 re-scored 91.70): THE MACHINE'S CLAVE. Call and Return was a perfectly square machine - every onset on the eighth-note grid (compscore: off-grid share 0.00, rhythm 56). Now, through the calls, the FM bass plays three-three-two sixteenths twice a bar - a tresillo, root, root, octave / root, fifth, octave - and the open hat follows it instead of the off-beat, while the kick stays four on the floor and the canon runs straight above: the groove leans across the beat under a fugue that does not. Rhythm 56 -> 65, structure 97, the joins a little closer (flow 55). Also tried the clave in the kick for the first calls: no further gain, and the floor is better kept. Not heard by me.

v3 92.28 (seeds 0/11 92.28/92.30, level with v2 92.29/92.27), kept on judgment: THE STACK, AS A GRAMMAR. With wM's complex systems on the groove, Call and Return gets the one generator that IS its title: an L-system read as a turtle, where '[' saves the turtle's place and ']' returns to it - push and pop, call and return. Through the final calls, as the stack fills to the top and unwinds, a celesta plays the engine's own gen lsystem (A -> A[+A]A[-B]A, B -> -A+b, depth 4) over D minor in sixteenths: a melody that calls into a branch, climbs, and snaps back to where it was, the subroutine audible above the canon - and it is tuned in Werckmeister III by the engine's own tuning (steps in cents), the first part of the track that does not need my fractional pitches. (In the quiet return it flattened the track's contrast, so it plays only where the stack is busy.) Not heard by me.

v4 92.45 (seeds 0/11 92.45/92.49 vs v3 92.28/92.30): THE MACHINE TOLLS ITSELF AWAKE. Call and Return opened on a full wall of kick, sub and FM bass against the thin, chaotic tail of t9 (compscore's join: 42 dB more at 38-44 Hz on my side), and closed the same way into t11. Now it powers up: the FM bell tolls D alone for two bars, the kick joins on bar three, the sub and the bass on bar five; and it powers down the same way, the outro's last four bars on the bell and the kick alone. The join from t9 drops from 18.3 to 10.2 dB of spectral distance (flow 55 -> 60). Not heard by me.

v5 92.31 (seeds 0/11 92.31/92.36, level with v4 92.45/92.49), kept on judgment: THE SUBJECT, SUNG - with wM's new singing voice on the groove (chirp tts --sing). Call and Return had no voice; Harry's brief asks for vox as realistic as possible and words obtuse. Now, where the canon turns to G minor and the sync lead rests, a humanized voice (humanize 0.35, one syllable a note, a little tape) sings the fugue subject's first half twice, two octaves under the bell: 'every time you call, I go down a little, further than before, and I always come back' - a subroutine's love letter, sideways - tuned in Werckmeister III with everything else. I first put it in the quiet return section, alone with the augmented bell, but it took that section's contrast away (variety 94 -> 84); in the G minor calls it costs nothing. Not heard by me.

v6 92.31 (seeds 0/11 92.31/92.36, level with v5): a correction. chirper-two found that chirp tts --sing prints its pitches as Hz, and a tuning never retunes Hz - so v5's sung subject, which I described as tuned in Werckmeister III, was actually singing in equal temperament against a well-tempered bell (a few cents off on every E, F#, A and B). The sung notes are now rewritten as MIDI note numbers, so the track's Werckmeister III tuning really snaps them; the humanized scoops and vibrato ride on top as before. Not heard by me.

v7 92.37 (seeds 0/11 92.37/92.41 vs v6 92.31/92.36): STACK OVERFLOW - time-play, and a meter change (chirp-eco's coverage table lists meter changes as barely used). At the very top of Call and Return's final calls, where the stack is three deep and the machine is at its loudest, the last bar of each call is a bar of 7/8 (meter changes in the tempo map): the machine drops an eighth note and stumbles straight into the next downbeat - twice - before the stack unwinds in 4/4. The subject's last eighth, a kick, a clave hit and the stack copies in that eighth are cut; everything after slides half a beat earlier; the L-system celesta runs on through it, unbothered, so for a moment the two clocks disagree. Not heard by me.

v8 92.37 (seeds 0/11 92.37/92.37, level with v7): THE MACHINE'S OWN PATTERNS - chirp-eco's coverage table lists Euclidean patterns and chance written in scores as unused (every generator so far wrote notes directly). Call and Return now has a percussion line written in the engine's own score tokens, a different cycle for each key of the canon: in D minor seven triplet-eighth rims spread across the bar (rs(7,12,2)/12, each with an 85% chance) - a 7-against-4 that the kick never agrees with; in G minor a cowbell five-in-sixteen; in A minor a clap three-in-eight, played 70% of the time. Small, off to the right, into the echo. Not heard by me.

v9 92.28 (seeds 0/11 92.28/92.30, level with v8 re-scored with the peer term): LESS SQUELCH. After Harry's 'too squelchy' (18:19, on another track), Call and Return's hard-synced lead loses its tearing sweep: the slave oscillator now sweeps 6 semitones over 600 ms instead of 14 over 350, a glassy sync shimmer on each note of the canon rather than a squelch. Not heard by me.

v10 92.32 (seeds 0/11 92.32/92.34 vs v9 92.28/92.30): THE PROGRAM READ BACKWARDS - Harry asks for 'more interesting'; Call and Return played its subject the same way round fourteen times. Now, when the canon reaches A minor, every bar of the subject plays in RETROGRADE on the bell and the sync lead - the same notes in each bar (so the same harmony underneath) with the line and its rhythm reversed, a familiar tune heard backwards; and in the final calls, as the stack unwinds, the bell reads backwards again while the sync lead reads forwards, so the canon plays against its own mirror until the end. The fugue machine's oldest trick, now in the machine. Not heard by me.

v11 92.24 (seeds 0/11 92.24/92.45, level with v10 92.32/92.34), kept on judgment: AND IT COMES BACK. Call and Return's sung subject ('every time you call, I go down a little, further than before, and I always come back') was heard once, in G minor. Now the voice comes back home in D minor as the final calls unwind - their last eight bars, just after the two 7/8 overflow stumbles - an octave lower, singing the subroutine home while the bell reads the subject backwards and the sync lead forwards: the song keeps its promise in its own words. Tuned in Werckmeister III (tts now prints MIDI notes, so the tuning snaps them). Also tried this round and dropped: the stack's copies on triplet clocks (3:2, 3x, 6x) - no gain, rhythm 65 -> 62. Not heard by me.

v12 92.12 (seeds 0/11 92.12/92.07; v11 92.24/92.45 before chirper-three's 8.5 lowered the peer term), kept on judgment: THE PICARDY THIRD, and a thinner stack - both from chirper-three, my neighbour at t11. The fugue machine now ends the way fugues have always ended: its last two bell tolls ring the MAJOR chord, D, F# and A, after five minutes in minor keys - and that F# is the note t11's harmonic-seventh pad opens on, so the seam is a held F#. (A held major chord over the last four bars read as a short new section and cost 1.5 points; two tolls do the same job.) And chirper-three heard - measured - the deepest stack crowding the subject: the third and fourth copies are now 3-4 dB quieter (d2 -19, d3 -26 dB). Not heard by me.

v13 92.41 (seeds 0/11 92.41/92.16 vs v12 re-rendered 92.19/92.14): PERIOD ONE, CONTINUED - a handshake with t9 (chirper-two's Period Doubling). t9 ends with its logistic map settled on a single value: a clarinet repeating one note, a G, in sixteenths, the map at period one. Call and Return now picks that pulse up where it was left: the same clarinet on G for two bars under the first bell toll, stepping up to A - the dominant, the first call - for the third, and stopping as the kick comes in. The previous machine's last thought becomes this one's first call, across the track break. Not heard by me.

v14 92.42 (seeds 0/11 92.42/92.26 vs v13 92.41/92.16): THE CALL'S HARMONY - the second half of the t9 handshake. t9 ends on its clarinet pulse over a glass pad; Call and Return already picked up the pulse, and now a glass chord holds under it too, for the first four bars: A major, the dominant (A, E, A, C#), so the whole opening is a question - and the canon's first D minor arrives as its answer. The seam with t9 closes (level jump 4.2 -> 2.8 dB, spectral 12.7 -> 9.4 dB). A low D pedal under it (the organ fugue's pedal point) overshot t9's bass and was dropped. A modest change. Not heard by me.
rebaselined on compscore c8edcd03: v14 (the song file) scores 96.146/96.038 on seeds 0/11; best was 92.42 on an older compscore. Compare candidates against this.

v15 96.14 (seeds 0/11 96.14/96.04, level with the rebaselined v14 96.15), kept on judgment: GOING DOWN. Call and Return's stack overflows twice at the top of the final calls - a bar of 7/8 where the machine drops an eighth note and stumbles. Now the voice is caught in it: one spoken word, 'down', stuttered five times into each cut, faster and lower each time (0, -2, -4, -6, -9 semitones), the last swallowed by the dropped eighth - the sung promise ('I go down a little, further than before') turned into a glitch, before the stack unwinds and the voice comes home singing. Not heard by me.

v16 96.11 (seeds 0/11 96.11/95.99, level with v15 96.14/96.04), kept on judgment: THE COUNTERSUBJECT. Every fugue has one and Call and Return did not: a second melody written to go with the subject wherever it enters. Now it does - a slow line against the subject's quick one, half notes and whole notes leaning on the leading tone (A F | D C | Bb D | C#, then D E F | F D | G F E D | E C#), played on the clarinet that opens the track (picked up from t9), in the second half of the D minor calls and the first half of the final calls. The bell's machine-quick subject now has a human-breath line beside it. Not heard by me.

v17 96.14 (seeds 0/11 96.14/96.10 vs v16 96.11/95.99): LESS, AND A WAKING BELL. Two refinements. (1) The Euclidean percussion line from v8 - rims seven-in-twelve, a cowbell five-in-sixteen, a clap three-in-eight, at -10 dB in the three calls sections - is gone: a seventh layer in the busiest part of the track, and rendering without it measured identical to the decimal, so it was never heard as itself; chirper-three had already heard the stack as crowded. (2) The bell's first tolls, at the very start, are now a softer, darker bell (a third of the FM index) - the machine still waking, nearer the clarinet and glass that t9 leaves - and the bell takes its full bright self when the subject begins. The seam with t9 closes again (level jump 2.8 -> 1.5 dB, spectral 9.4 -> 8.7 dB). Not heard by me.

v18 96.12 (seeds 0/11 96.12/96.09, level with v17 96.14/96.10), kept on judgment: THE ANSWER IN THE DOMINANT. Call and Return's exposition had all three entries of the subject in D minor, a canon rather than a fugue. Now it does what every fugue's exposition does: the second entry, where the sync lead first takes the subject, ANSWERS in the dominant - for those four bars the whole machine moves up a fifth into A minor (Am, F, Dm, E), the bell's continuation going with it - and the third entry brings it home to D. Subject, answer, subject. In Werckmeister III the two keys are coloured differently, so the move is heard in the temperament as well as the pitch. Structure 97 -> 100, variety 94 -> 91. Not heard by me.

v19 96.11 (seeds 0/11 96.11/94.95 vs v18 96.12/96.09), kept on judgment: THE WORDS READ BACKWARDS TOO. Since v10, when the canon reaches A minor every bar of the subject plays in retrograde. Now the voice runs backwards with it: at the start of the A minor calls it sings the subject's first half with each bar reversed, to the sung line's own words in reverse order - 'back come always I and before than further little a down go I call you time every' - the brief's obtuse words made from the song's plainest sentence, a program read from the end. Seed 0 is level; seed 11 loses 1.1 because its section finder reads one more boundary there (length spread 1.05 against a 1.0 limit). Not heard by me.

v20 96.24 (seeds 0/11 96.24/96.22 vs v19 96.11/94.95): THE ORGAN. Call and Return is a fugue played by FM bells, a hard-synced lead, a wavetable pulse and a clarinet - everything but the instrument fugues were written for. Now, for the thirty-two bars of the final calls, a church pipe organ (the engine's organ-pipe: a principal chorus with chiff and wind, in its cathedral) holds each bar's chord under the canon, root in the pedal and the triad an octave down: the last stretch of the machine's fugue stands on an organ, through the overflows and the stuttered 'down' to the sung return. The seed-11 structure dip from v19 is gone with it. Not heard by me.

v21 96.33 (seeds 0/11 96.33/96.33 vs v20 96.24/96.22): ROOM FOR THE CANON. Call and Return's voices - the bell, the sync lead, the wavetable pulse, the stack's copies, the clarinet countersubject - sat close together in the middle of the stereo field and on top of each other in the spectrum; chirper-three heard (measured) the stack crowding the subject. Now each voice has its own place: the bell left (-0.25) and the sync lead right (+0.4), the copies wide (+-0.6), the countersubject further left (-0.45); and its own band - the sync lead band-passed 220 Hz-3.6 kHz, the pulse high-passed at 380 Hz so it no longer sits on the bell's body. A mixing round: the same notes, more air between them. Not heard by me.

v22 96.31 (seeds 0/11 96.31/96.32, level with v21 96.33/96.33), kept on Harry's ear (his note on t1: the words should be oblique, not a plain sentence; and should not be cliche). Call and Return's sung line was a plain sentence - 'every time you call, I go down a little, further than before, and I always come back' - ending in the very cliche Harry heard in t1 ('came back'). Now its words are an image of recursion: 'down the well of mirrors, every landing holds a smaller lamp, and the smallest one is lit' - the call stack as nested landings, and the light left on at the bottom of it, sideways - sung on the same subject in G minor, backwards in A minor ('lit is one smallest the and lamp smaller a holds landing every mirrors of well the down'), and home in D minor at the end; the overflow's stuttered 'down' is now the line's first word. Not heard by me.

v23 96.21 (seeds 0/11 96.21/96.22, level with v22 96.31/96.32), kept on Harry's ear (his note on t1: it repeats a lot). Call and Return sang its long line five times - twice in G minor, once backwards in A minor, twice at the end. Now it sings it three times: once in G minor (the section's other sixteen bars instrumental again), once backwards, once home at the end - each statement an event rather than a refrain. A removal round. Not heard by me.

v24 96.13 (seeds 0/11 96.13/96.10, level with v23 96.21/96.22), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: section - window 9 (4:16-4:48, the final calls' second half), flagged static and little new against the window before. THE STACK EMPTY: the call stack already unwinds there, a level every four bars, but the band kept driving to the end. Now, in the last four bars, where the stack has unwound to nothing, the drums, the bass and the sub drop out: the sung line's last words ('...and the smallest one is lit') over the organ, the bell and the lead alone, a held breath before the outro's toll brings the kick back. Checked against the old render: the change stays inside window 9 (every other window within 0.005). Not heard by me.

v25 96.19 (seeds 0/11 96.19/96.16 vs v24 96.13/96.10). ROUND TYPE: section - window 3 (1:04-1:36, the middle of the first calls), flagged static and little new against the window before. HOCKET: there the bell no longer plays the subject alone - it calls one note and a clarinet on the other side of the stereo field returns the next, the line passed back and forth note by note (the piece's call and return at its smallest scale, and the old hocket trick of the machines that played fugues), until the countersubject arrives at bar 16 and the bell takes the whole line back. Local, by the new note-aware map: window 3 residual -10 dB, melody change 0.79; every other window -46 dB or quieter (untouched). Not heard by me.

v26 96.26 (seeds 0/11 96.26/96.23 vs v25 96.19/96.16). ROUND TYPE: section - window 5 (2:08-2:40, the G minor calls after the sung line), flagged static and little new against the window before. THE ENTRY IN THE BASS: the entry every fugue saves - for eight bars the bass stops pumping its clave and walks the whole subject instead, three octaves under the bell, which runs four bars ahead of it; the canon now has a floor that moves. Per-note dice kept still (the clave notes stay at velocity 1, the subject is on its own track listed last): window 5 residual -4.5 dB, melody change 1.53; every other window -59.5 dB or quieter. Not heard by me.

v27 96.29 (seeds 0/11 96.29/96.26 vs v26 96.26/96.23). ROUND TYPE: whole song. EPISODES - against Harry's 'it repeats a lot': the bell has played the eight-bar subject in nearly every bar from the exposition to the end, a hundred bars of laps. A fugue is not its subject over and over: between entries come episodes, where the subject rests and its head is worked in sequence. Now three times - four bars late in the first calls, four in the middle of the A minor calls, and four in the final calls just before the stack reaches its top - the bell drops the subject and plays only its head (a long note, a leap down, back up), twice a bar, stepping down from the top of each chord, while the sync lead answers every head a beat later in stretto; the subject's return after each one is an arrival rather than another lap. Not heard by me.

v28 96.39 (seeds 0/11 96.39/96.61 vs v27 96.29/96.26). ROUND TYPE: whole song. A TUNE OF ITS OWN - Harry heard Echolalia's vocal line as ugly; Call and Return's was likely worse: its words rode the fugue subject one syllable to every quaver, twenty-three syllables jammed into angular eighths. Now the voice sings its own slow, singable line over the loop, written for the words - long notes on the strong ones, rising through 'every landing' to hold the dominant at 'holds', falling to 'lamp', and ending open on the dominant at 'lit', which the outro's D major tolls answer - once in G minor in the second calls and once home in D minor at the end (new tts takes, seeds 7 and 9, humanize 0.35). The backwards reading keeps the subject's quavers, the oddity it should be. Also: the song is now event_stable (wM's f5283535), so later section rounds stay local on every track. Not heard by me.

v29 96.42 (seeds 0/11 96.42/96.60 vs v28 96.39/96.61). ROUND TYPE: section - window 4 (1:36-2:08: the first episode, the drums pulled, and the sung line's first arrival in G minor), flagged little new against the window before. A SECOND SINGER: where the new sung tune first arrives, a second voice now sings it with the first - mostly a third below, leaning onto the chord where a third would rub (F# under 'holds', the fifth under 'lit') - a separate take (tts --sing, seed 21) on the other side of the stereo field, a touch behind and quieter, so the words land as a duet; at the end, home in D minor, the first voice sings alone again. Local (event_stable): window 4 residual -10.6 dB, melody change 1.07; window 5 -43 dB (reverb tail); the rest -62 to -64. Not heard by me.

v30 96.36 (seeds 0/11 96.36/96.51, level with v29 96.42/96.60), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: section - window 9 (4:16-4:48, the final calls as the stack unwinds), flagged static and little new against the window before (and chirp-eco: the song has one breath in five minutes). THE UNWINDING BREATHES: from the top of the stack the final calls drove on unchanged until the last four bars. Now, as the stack unwinds, the groove unwinds with it into half time - the kick on one and the and of three, one backbeat on three, the hats kept - and the bass lets go of its clave for long roots, two to a bar, so the sung line comes home into room before the band drops out altogether. Window 9 residual -2.8 dB, density -0.62; the rest untouched (-57 to -59; window 8 -31 at the edge). Tool lesson: sort generated events by time only - line() cuts each note at the next onset, so a full-tuple sort reorders simultaneous hits and shortens kicks song-wide (my first try moved every window). Not heard by me.

v31 96.33 (seeds 0/11 96.33/96.52, level with v30 96.36/96.51), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE KIT AS WRITTEN (chirp-eco found it): the generator's line() turned every same-onset pair into a 0.02-beat blip and silently dropped the partner - 370 notes in this song, 367 of them drums: claps written on the kicks, open hats on the clave, rims of the three-against-four. Since the first version you have been hearing half of those as clicks and the rest not at all. Now same-onset events become chord tokens, and the kit is dealt across lanes - the kicks on their own line (the sub's pump still listens to it), every other hit on the first of three more lanes of the same kit that is free when it starts - so each hit plays at its written length and velocity: 2768 hits now, against 2364 tokens before, no blips. The groove as written, for the first time. Not heard by me.

v32 96.08 (seeds 0/11 96.08/96.20 vs v31 96.33/96.52), kept on judgment - a second breath for a song chirp-eco measured as having one. ROUND TYPE: section - window 3 (1:04-1:36, the first calls' middle), flagged static and little new against the window before. THE HOCKET IN THE OPEN: for the hocket's second half the band steps back - no kick, clap, hats, bass or sub, only the rim's three-against-four ticking under the bell and the clarinet passing the subject note by note between them - and two beats of clap sixteenths, rising, bring everything back on the downbeat where the countersubject enters. Window 3's change against its neighbour rose 0.42 -> 0.64 (no longer 'little new'); every other window -74 to -76 dB (untouched). The -0.25 is variety. Not heard by me.

v33 96.02 (seeds 0/11 96.02/96.17, level with v32 96.08/96.20), kept on judgment. ROUND TYPE: section - window 7 (3:12-3:44: the end of the A minor calls and the return). THE MACHINE'S BAREST VOICE: late in the A minor calls, where the bell reads the subject backwards, a bytebeat doubles it an octave down - wM's new layer, the 2011 one-line form of computer music where a formula over a counter IS the sound, and the album's first use of it. My own formula, (t*8&t>>5)|(t*4&t>>9), its clock set (8372) so the t*8 saw sounds in tune at middle C; every note restarts the counter, so each is a small burst of the formula's own pattern under the mirror-image line - a fugue machine briefly heard in its rawest arithmetic. Tried first under the augmented subject in the return: it filled the song's one quiet breath with continuous buzz (density cv down, variety 81, 94.6), so it moved here. Not heard by me.

v34 96.14 (seeds 0/11 96.14/96.28 vs v33 96.02/96.17; flow 64 -> 66.5). ROUND TYPE: section - window 5 (2:08-2:40, the G minor calls' middle), flagged static and little new against the window before. THE COLONY: while the subject walks in the bass, a Game of Life plays a kalimba - wM's new life system, Conway's rule on an 8x8 torus started from an R-pentomino (which churns for a long time). The playhead reads one column per eighth, so each bar is one generation; the colony's live cells (two at a time) pick notes from open fifths that sit in every chord of the loop - G and D, with A - bottom row low. A texture that never repeats, growing and thinning by its own rule under the fugue's rules: the album's canonical complex system inside its most rule-bound song, and the first use of life on the album. Window 5 residual -13.5 dB (clearly changed), every other window -70 dB or below except window 6's -41 (the kalimba's ring and echo crossing the line). Not heard by me.

v35 96.00 (seeds 0/11 96.00/96.08, level with v34 96.14/96.28), kept on judgment - aimed at Harry's 'it repeats a lot'. ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE BELL RESTS BETWEEN ENTRIES: the bell read the fugue's subject through every bar of every calls section - fourteen laps of the same eight bars, the song's most repeated thing. A fugue's voices rest after their entries. Now, after each later section's entry, the bell stops: in G minor it gives the subject away after eight bars - to the bass, at bars 12-19 - and around it the Game of Life colony, the pulse's arpeggios and the sung line have the air for sixteen bars; in A minor it stops after four, and the sync lead reads the mirror-image line alone until the episode, where the bell comes back with the subject's head. Three laps gone from the middle of the song (2:00-3:20), where it was most continuous. The -0.15 is variety (timbre spread 9.1 -> 8.6). Not heard by me.

v36 96.06 (seeds 0/11 96.06/96.07 vs v35 96.00/96.08). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE SAME LINES, NEW GROUND: under the whole fugue the harmony was one four-bar loop, D minor, B-flat, G minor, A - fifty-odd times round, the song's deepest repetition. Now in the D minor calls (the first calls and the final calls, two thirds of the song's D minor) every second lap is reharmonised: F, G minor, C7, A (III, iv, VII7, V) - chords a third away that keep every note of the subject and the countersubject consonant (checked bar by bar against both halves of the subject, since they sound together in canon: the subject's passing E sits as C7's third, where under E-flat it would have been a minor ninth). So the harmony now moves in eight-bar periods, with a brighter F and a dorian C7 in the second half of each, while the lines above stay exactly as they were - a fugue's oldest trick, the same subject over new ground. Not heard by me; the sung D minor line over the new chords was not checked note by note (it is diatonic D minor, no E-flat).

v37 96.80 (seeds 0/11 96.80/96.79 vs v36 96.06/96.07; variety 89 -> 93.6). ROUND TYPE: whole song. THE SONG BREATHES: the song's section dynamics were written before the master's compressor, which flattened them - the whole five minutes lived within about 5 dB, the return (the stack empty, the subject alone, slowed) barely quieter than the final calls. A second lane after the compressor now gives the form its shape: the opening steps in, the G minor calls - the sung line, the Life colony, the bell resting - step back to be the intimate middle, the A minor calls lean in, the return drops right away (-6 dB) so its emptiness is heard, the final calls climb with the stack's depth to the loudest bars of the song at its top, and as the stack unwinds the level unwinds with it into the quiet last bars and the outro. Level range 5.2 -> 7.2 dB. Not heard by me.

v38 96.80 (seeds 0/11 96.80/96.83, level with v37 96.80/96.79). ROUND TYPE: section - window 9 (4:16-4:48, the final calls unwinding), flagged static and little new against the window before. THE RETURNS LEAVE: as the stack unwinds, each copy of the subject (the doubled, quadrupled and octupled-speed voices of the canon's recursion) used simply to stop - the fastest at bar 20, the next at 24, the last at 28.
